Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create a NEW module. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 5 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/transcript_quotes.py
  tests/test_transcript_quotes.py

WHY. Show notes must quote the guest's OWN words with a speaker and a timestamp
(server/pipeline/show_notes_structure.build_show_notes RAISES on a quote missing either,
because an unattributed quote is how invented content reaches a published page). Nothing
currently extracts them, so quotes have to be hand-picked. This module supplies candidates
deterministically from the transcript.

TRANSCRIPT FORMAT (real, from processed/transcript.txt) — one utterance per line:
    [00:12:11] Guest: optometrists, it was 54%. I mean, that's every other optometrist listening in right now,
    [00:12:18] Guest: potentially facing some level of burnout. And so that's kind of my message is to, you know,
    [00:15:16] Host: So tell me something tactically you were like...
Speaker labels are "Host" and "Guest". Lines are mid-sentence fragments: a sentence
routinely spans several lines, so extraction MUST join consecutive same-speaker lines before
splitting into sentences, or every quote will be a fragment.

BUILD server/pipeline/transcript_quotes.py — stdlib only, deterministic:

  parse_transcript(text) -> list[{"timestamp_s": float, "speaker": str, "text": str}]
      Parse [HH:MM:SS] and the speaker label. Lines that do not match are skipped, not
      guessed at. Preserve order.

  merge_utterances(entries) -> list[...]
      Join consecutive entries from the SAME speaker into one block, keeping the FIRST
      entry's timestamp (when the speaker started talking).

  extract_quote_candidates(text, *, speaker="Guest", limit=6,
                           min_words=MIN_QUOTE_WORDS, max_words=MAX_QUOTE_WORDS)
        -> list[{"text","timestamp_s","speaker"}]
      From merged blocks of the requested speaker, split into sentences and return the
      best standalone candidates. Each candidate carries the timestamp of the block it came
      from. Named constants with rationale: MIN_QUOTE_WORDS = 8 (shorter is not a quote),
      MAX_QUOTE_WORDS = 45 (longer will not fit a show-notes blockquote).
      SCORING, highest first, all deterministic — no randomness:
        + first person ("I", "my", "we") — the guest talking about themselves
        + a concrete number or percentage
        + a complete sentence (starts with a capital or 'I', ends with . ! or ?)
        - starts with a discourse marker (so, and, but, well, yeah, okay, um, uh, like)
        - contains a filler run ("you know", "kind of", "sort of", "I mean")
        - is mostly a question (show-notes quotes should be statements)
      Return at most `limit`, de-duplicated, in descending score then ascending timestamp.
      CLEANING: strip leading discourse markers and trailing incomplete clauses, collapse
      whitespace, but NEVER change a word the speaker said and never join text across a
      speaker change. Fabrication risk is the whole point of this module.

  extract_highlight_candidates(text, *, limit=8) -> list[{"timestamp_s","label"}]
      Coarse chapter markers: take merged HOST blocks that look like questions (the host
      asking a question usually opens a topic), label them with a short cleaned phrase from
      that question, and return evenly-spread candidates across the episode duration so the
      highlights are not clustered in the first five minutes.

TESTS (tests/test_transcript_quotes.py; at least 5). Use REAL transcript excerpts pasted as
fixtures, including the multi-line 54% passage above:
 (1) a sentence split across three consecutive Guest lines is returned as ONE complete quote
     with the timestamp of the first line — the core requirement;
 (2) every returned candidate has a non-empty text, a float timestamp_s, and speaker "Guest";
 (3) NEGATIVE: a Host line adjacent to Guest lines never appears in Guest quotes, and text is
     never joined across the speaker change;
 (4) NEGATIVE: candidates below MIN_QUOTE_WORDS or above MAX_QUOTE_WORDS are excluded;
 (5) scoring: a first-person sentence containing "54%" outranks a filler-heavy sentence of
     the same length;
 (6) determinism: calling twice on the same input returns identical output;
 (7) malformed lines (no timestamp, no speaker) are skipped without raising;
 (8) highlight candidates are spread across the timeline rather than all under 300s.
tasks.verified: deterministic timestamped guest quotes and spread highlights, joined across multi-line utterances, never across a speaker change

Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production change with no tests, fewer than 5 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these):
  server/pipeline/show_notes.py
  tests/test_show_notes_default_structure.py
  tests/test_show_notes.py

WHAT EXISTS. server/pipeline/show_notes_structure.py already provides the canonical
structure and is proven on a real episode: SECTIONS, REQUIRED_SECTIONS, build_show_notes(),
render_markdown(), validate_show_notes(). It is NOT yet used by the pipeline. Today
server/pipeline/show_notes.py stores freeform notes in episode.json under
show_notes.<kind> ({summary, highlights, episode_description, status, ...}) and its private
_render_md(ep) writes an ad-hoc markdown file to content/show-notes.md. The owner's
instruction: make the structure the DEFAULT.

THE WIRING:
1. Add build_structured_notes(ep, kind="publish") -> dict that assembles the canonical
   structure from what the episode already holds:
     - episode_number and title from episode data (content/episode_content.json content
       block when present, else episode.json) — read what actually exists, do not invent
       a source;
     - hook from the stored notes summary's FIRST sentence;
     - highlights: prefer stored timestamped highlights; when the stored highlights are
       plain strings with no timestamp, fall back to
       server.pipeline.transcript_quotes.extract_highlight_candidates over
       processed/transcript.txt;
     - quotes: server.pipeline.transcript_quotes.extract_quote_candidates(speaker="Guest");
     - guest: name/title/bio/links from the episode's first guest record; pass the guest's
       email through UNCHANGED so show_notes_structure applies its own share_email rule —
       do not re-implement that privacy decision here;
     - booking_link=server.config.HUBSPOT_MEETING_LINK, show_url=server.config.PODCAST_SHOW_URL
       read from config, never literals;
     - headshot from the guest record's photo/headshot field when present.
   Import transcript_quotes lazily and degrade gracefully if the transcript file is absent.
2. _render_md(ep) uses the structured path BY DEFAULT: build_structured_notes then
   show_notes_structure.render_markdown. If the structured build raises (for example no
   quote carries a timestamp), do NOT silently fall back to the old freeform renderer:
   write the freeform output but record the failure on the notes block as
   structure_error=<message> and log a warning, so the gap is visible rather than hidden.
   Keep the old renderer available as _render_md_legacy for that path and for tests.
3. The publish QA gate (run_show_notes_qa / apply_show_notes_qa_gate) additionally runs
   show_notes_structure.validate_show_notes on the structured notes when they built, and a
   non-empty problem list FAILS the gate with the problems in the reason, routing to
   review-required. Preserve every existing QA rule; this is additive.
4. Keep save_show_notes / approve_show_notes signatures unchanged. Existing callers must
   not need edits.

TESTS (tests/test_show_notes_default_structure.py, pure with tmp_path episodes and a small
synthetic transcript; at least 5):
 (1) rendered markdown for a well-formed episode contains the canonical section headings,
     the booking link from config, and a quote with a timestamp — proving structured is the
     DEFAULT path, not opt-in;
 (2) the booking link in the output equals server.config.HUBSPOT_MEETING_LINK (no literal);
 (3) NEGATIVE: when the structured build cannot succeed (no transcript and no timestamped
     quotes) the file is still written via the legacy renderer AND structure_error is
     recorded on the notes block — assert both, proving the failure is visible not silent;
 (4) NEGATIVE: validate problems (inject a 42-word run-on into the summary) FAIL the publish
     QA gate and set status review-required, with the problem text in the reason;
 (5) the guest email does not appear in rendered output by default, and does when the guest
     record sets share_email;
 (6) save_show_notes and approve_show_notes still work with their current signatures.
Keep the existing tests/test_show_notes.py green; update any assertion that pinned the old
freeform markdown with a one-line comment explaining the default changed.
tasks.verified: canonical structure is the default render and gate; a structured-build failure is recorded, never silently hidden
